lead_headline: Lost Coffee opens sixth Colorado shop in Arvada while Heretik debuts French-Spanish rotisserie in RiNo — 11 new restaurant leads tracked

restaurant.blurb: 11 new leads today: Heretik (Adley's French-Spanish rotisserie in RiNo), Petunia Bakeshop (Sunnyside relocation), Flaming Grill (Indian fusion downtown), Pelican Bay closure at Cherry Creek.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications for the fifth straight day — the post-flood freeze extends through Friday, now marking eight consecutive filing-free days since the April 29-30 backend dumped 2,144 mass renewals. The 7-day rolling total remains locked at 0 versus last week's 2,386-application deluge, exposing a 100% collapse from the normal 20-30 weekly baseline. This eight-day drought now points to either sustained backend processing delays or a deliberate hold following the flood. State licensing officials have offered no public comment on the pause, leaving May's pipeline status unclear — applications may be queued offline awaiting batch release, or the system could be undergoing post-flood cleanup. The silence grows more conspicuous with each passing day.

reputation.blurb: 4 mentions today (Facebook, Instagram business features) push the 7-day total to 53 across 8 sources, up 18% from last week's 45 and breaking the five-day lull. Instagram leads with 15 mentions (28% share), followed by Denver Post (17), Facebook (11), and X (4), while Broomfield downtown development coverage drove today's activity. The 53-mention pace runs 18% above last week and 8% above the 30-day rolling average of 49 — outlets are emerging from mid-week coast mode. Social platforms still dominate discovery (52 via Google News RSS, 1 via Reddit), but traditional outlet pickups are creeping back into rotation. The week's momentum shift suggests Friday editorial desks are returning to normal cadence.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) extends MTD to +17 (+2.4/day) and holds 90-day net at +133. The single-add day marks the seventh consecutive cancellation-free session to open May — the longest zero-churn streak in recent memory. This week's +17 net (21 new, 4 canceled) dwarfs last week's +0 (21 new, 21 canceled), with acquisition volume matching but churn collapsing 81%. MTD's +2.4/day rate runs 71% ahead of the YTD +1.4/day baseline, and the pattern shows May absorbing April 28th's −13 crater while establishing cleaner momentum. The seven-day churn freeze is building unusual cushion — either retention mechanisms are clicking or we're entering a seasonal calm before renewal cycles resume.
